supporting_observations.claim: At 13:49:16 UTC, FILE-PIN-01 sent 640,000,367 bytes to PROXY-PIN-01 on port 8080; the connection lasted about 16 seconds. This is the observed large transfer relevant to the alert.
A separate, smaller FILE-PIN-01 connection to the same proxy occurred shortly before the large transfer.

The transfer’s size is consistent with the inventory description of approved Vaultline backups, but the available connection record does not identify the destination service or the process that sent the data.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-PIN-01 winsec and Sysmon telemetry was not collected during the review window, so process attribution and host-side activity for the transfer are unavailable.
PROXY-PIN-01 proxy logs were not collected during the review window, so the proxy request’s destination, URL, and service identity cannot be verified.
Zeek connection telemetry records the transfer to the internal proxy, not the ultimate external destination.
claims_not_established: Whether the 640 MB transfer was made by the approved Vaultline backup agent or another process.
Whether the transfer reached vaultline-backup.com or an unapproved destination.
Whether the transfer was an authorized backup or data exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy transaction logs for the connection beginning at 2026-09-08 13:49:16 UTC, including the requested destination and request metadata.
Obtain FILE-PIN-01 process execution and network telemetry for the transfer, including process path, command line, user, and parent process.
Review Vaultline agent logs and backup job history around 13:49 UTC, and confirm the expected destination and amount of data uploaded.
If available, review egress firewall or NAT records to identify the external endpoint associated with the proxy transaction.
unrelated_findings: PROXY-PIN-01 attempted several connections to FILE-PIN-01 on ports 22, 80, and 135 that were rejected, then established an RDP connection. This is separate from the alerted transfer and merits review under the organization’s remote-administration policy. (T070-00398, T070-00399, T070-00400, T070-00401)

FILE-PIN-01 generated NTLM authentication for emma.stone to WS-ESTONE-01 during the window. The available records do not establish why; review separately. (T070-00169, T070-00170, T070-00264, T070-00265)

A PowerShell process on WS-TWEBER-01 used explicit svc-billing credentials against FILE-PIN-01 after the scheduled password-rotation time. This relates to billing-job maintenance, not the alerted transfer, and merits separate validation. (T070-00433)
